topStories.headline: Empire Theater Site Proposal Nearly Triples in Size, Sparking New West Portal Battle
topStories.dek: A 12-story, 172-unit apartment tower has been proposed for 85 West Portal Avenue — nearly triple the 64-unit plan unveiled just months ago — reigniting debate over density and neighborhood character.
topStories.body:
A development that first surfaced in early 2026 as a modest nine-story, 64-unit project on the site of the shuttered Empire Theater at 85 West Portal Avenue has been dramatically expanded. The revised proposal, filed by DM Development on behalf of property owner Empire West Portal LLC, now calls for a 12-story mixed-use building with 172 rental apartments above ground-floor retail and a basement garage — nearly tripling the original unit count.

The expansion was made possible by Mayor Daniel Lurie's recently enacted 'Family Zoning' changes, which allow greater residential density on commercial parcels, as well as the acquisition of an adjacent property at 61 West Portal Avenue that previously housed a Goodwill and Supercuts. The new application also leans on Assembly Bill 1287 and Senate Bill 423 to maximize height and density beyond what local zoning would otherwise allow.

The revised plan includes 26 deed-restricted affordable units — half targeted at 'very low income' households and half at moderate-income families — out of the 172-unit total. The theater at 85 West Portal, most recently known as CineArts at the Empire, has been closed since early 2021.

Neighborhood reaction has been divided. The West Portal Merchants Association had gathered more than 1,300 petition signatures opposing even the smaller nine-story version earlier this year. With the project now nearly three times its original size, a more sustained fight appears likely, mirroring similar battles playing out across San Francisco's western neighborhoods as state and local housing laws override traditional zoning limits.

topStories.headline: SFMTA Completes Final Beautification Phase at West Portal Station This Week
topStories.dek: Decorative crosswalks are being painted this week at Ulloa Street and West Portal Avenue, wrapping up the multi-year safety and community space improvement project at the neighborhood's central transit hub.
topStories.body:
The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency announced that crews are painting decorative crosswalks at West Portal Station beginning the week of September 2 — the final piece of a multi-phase safety and beautification project that was set in motion after a driver struck and killed a family of four at a bus stop near the station in March 2024.

Crew will paint decorative crosswalks at all crosswalks at the Ulloa Street and West Portal Avenue intersection, as well as a decorative crosswalk on Ulloa Street crossing Lenox Way. Work is being performed late at night to minimize disruptions, and is expected to take two nights, with up to six nights as a contingency. Hernandez Engineering is the contractor. Parking spaces will be temporarily reserved on Lenox Way and on Ulloa Street between West Portal Avenue and Claremont Boulevard during the work.

The crosswalks are the last elements in a project that has also delivered a street mural, 'Welcome to West Portal' station murals, drought-tolerant planters, a Bay Wheels bikeshare station — the first in the West Portal neighborhood — and traffic safety changes including turn restrictions and a pedestrian crossing beacon on Ulloa at Wawona streets. The horseshoe area at the station entrance was redesigned into a welcoming pedestrian plaza.

Data released by SFMTA in a June 2026 evaluation report found that the traffic and safety changes have been effective: traffic collision rates in the area dropped 60 percent between October 2024 and March 2026 compared with a comparable pre-project window, and the number of collisions resulting in serious injury fell from 6.7 per year to 2.7 per year.

topStories.headline: GatorFest 2026 Kicks Off at SFSU With Months of Campus Events
topStories.dek: San Francisco State University's annual welcome celebration launched this week with more than two months of activities for new and returning students, running through November 20.
topStories.body:
San Francisco State University's GatorFest 2026 is underway, bringing new and returning students together for an extended series of events stretching from late August through Friday, November 20. The annual celebration is designed to help students find community, discover campus resources, and settle into life at SFSU and San Francisco.

The opening weeks included an outdoor dance party called Noise Complaint, the Fall Pinning Ceremony for incoming students, an ice cream reception, Drag Queen Bingo, and a block party. Now that fall classes are in session, GatorFest activities continue with two weeks of 'Meet the Org' events on Malcolm X Plaza, where students can find clubs and organizations to join. Sports Club Week features a pep rally and a Greeks vs. Sports Clubs field day. A September outing to cheer on the San Francisco Giants is also on the schedule.

Upcoming GatorFest events open to SFSU students this month include Meet the Black Greeks on Malcolm X Plaza (September 3), and further programming through October including an alcohol awareness workshop, a Sound Bath Workshop, and a murder mystery game night. Students are encouraged to check the full schedule at the SFSU Student Activities website and RSVP via GatorXperience.

SFSU will be closed on Monday, September 7 in observance of Labor Day. Fall 2026 semester classes are fully underway.

moreNews.headline: Yellowstone Real Estate Seizes Parkmerced Development Parcels Through Foreclosure
moreNews.body: In a transaction completed in late July 2026, New York-based Yellowstone Real Estate Investments took control of four land parcels at Parkmerced through foreclosure. The parcels, which make up the first four subphases of a long-delayed redevelopment plan, are entitled for nearly 1,700 new apartments and also contain 52 existing units. Yellowstone had provided a $101 million construction loan to prior developer Maximus Real Estate Partners; that loan had ballooned to more than $199 million with accrued interest by the time of the foreclosure sale. The rest of the 3,200-plus-unit Parkmerced complex remains under the management of receiver Douglas Wilson Cos. and property manager Ballast.

moreNews.headline: Hardware Coffee Co. Opens in Former Papenhausen Hardware Space on West Portal
moreNews.body: Hardware Coffee Co. opened its West Portal location in May 2026 at 32 West Portal Ave, taking over the site of the beloved Papenhausen Hardware store. The all-day café serves coffee, beer and wine, and includes a full-service florist and light retail, as well as space for private events. The SF Standard named the café among West Portal's new dining destinations in a June 2026 feature on the neighborhood's restaurant boom.

moreNews.headline: Stonestown Galleria Redevelopment: Phase 1 Infrastructure Work Set to Begin
moreNews.body: The $2 billion Brookfield Properties redevelopment of Stonestown Galleria, approved by the San Francisco Board of Supervisors in July 2024, is in its pre-construction permit phase, with infrastructure work for Phase 1 anticipated to begin in 2026 per the approved development timeline. Phase 1 focuses on the underutilized parking area in the northwest corner of the 43-acre site, and includes new infrastructure, three- to four-story townhomes, adjacent parks and pathways, and a Town Square. The 775,000-square-foot mall will remain open throughout construction. The full buildout — up to 3,500 housing units, 160,000 square feet of new retail, and 100,000 square feet of office — is projected to unfold over 15 to 25 years.
